newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares plunge after hitting all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares plunge after hitting all-time high.

text.p: Greek shares reversed a firm opening on Tuesday which took the bourse's benchmark index to a new historic high at 1,695.03 and shed 2.90 percent in what brokers described as a rush to lock in capital gains.
The Athens general index settled a net 48.52 points lower to 1,621.71 from Monday's close of 1,670.23, recovering from an intra-day low of 1,608.80, touched a few minutes before close.
It had opened on a firm note after Prime Minister Costas Simitis told parliament on Monday that CPI inflation was seen easing below 5.5 percent in May from 5.9 percent in April.
Industrials led the decline with a 4.92 percent drop, followed by banks and construction which lost 2.30 and 1.74 percent respectively.
Brokers viewed the downturn as the result of concentrated selling pressure after certain technical target levels were reached.
"The sharp drop resulted from pure en-masse profit-taking after the index hit a new all-time high, a target level for many investors," said John Markopoulos, managing director at Sigma Securities.
The reaction to Tuesday's large drop in prices will set the stage for the market's near term prospects.
"Wednesday's session will be rather critical in the sense that the extent of the follow-up on Tuesday's profit-taking will set the market's short-term trend," Markopoulos said.
Other market participants said the downturn was the result of concern after the index stalled when it recorded a new all-time high.

"Selling was triggered by the lack of momentum to sustain the rally after the index topped its all-time high. Investors chose to realise their gains rather than risk price fluctuations," said a floor trader at a major brokerage.
Turnover soared to 41.5 billion drachmas in volume of 10.4 million shares, helped by a total of 1.8 million shares of Attica Enterprises traded in eight blocks at 2,200 drachmas.
Other blocks trades included Intracom, National Bank, Ionian Bank IOIr.AT, Aluminium of Attica, Metrolife and Doudos.
Decliners led advancers 170 to 64 with 21 stocks unchanged on 255 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 1,088-1,118. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, lost 150 drachmas to 6,400.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted lower at 651.49-693.08. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $86.54-$88.24. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 3,236-3,454 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $20.72-22.42. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted lower at 264-297 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
